title: Arduino as ISP
description: Turn your Arduino into a programmer and use it to put a bootloader on a bare ATmega328P chip.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × ATmega328P chip, 1 × 16 MHz crystal, 2 × 22 pF capacitor, 1 × 10 µF capacitor, 3 × 220 Ω resistor, 3 × LED, and some jumper wires.
Push the ATmega328P chip in across the middle gap, the notch (the little half-moon dent) on the left.
hints: With the notch on the left, pin 1 is bottom-left. Pins 1–14 run left to right along the bottom, 15–28 come back along the top.
Press gently on both ends so all 28 legs go in straight.
steps.goal: Put the chip on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. Chip pin 7 (VCC) → that same row.
hints: VCC is the chip's power in.
Count from pin 1 (bottom-left): along the bottom to 14, then back along the top from 15 on the right.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 7 (VCC) to 5V.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. Chip pin 8 (GND) → that same row.
hints: The chip's ground.
Count from pin 1 (bottom-left): along the bottom to 14, then back along the top from 15 on the right.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 8 (GND) to GND.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 20 (AVCC) to the red + row.
hints: AVCC powers the chip's analog side — it needs 5V too.
Count from pin 1 (bottom-left): along the bottom to 14, then back along the top from 15 on the right.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 20 (AVCC) to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 22 (GND) to the blue − row.
hints: The chip's second ground pin — connect both.
Count from pin 1 (bottom-left): along the bottom to 14, then back along the top from 15 on the right.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 22 (GND) to GND.

steps.clip: Push the 16 MHz crystal (the small silver can) in to the right of the chip, its two legs in two columns next to each other.
hints: The crystal is the chip's clock. It works either way round.
steps.goal: Put the crystal on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 9 to the crystal's left leg.
hints: Chip pin 9 is the 9th leg from the left on the bottom row.
Either crystal leg is fine — it has no + or −.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 9 to the crystal.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 10 to the crystal's right leg.
hints: Chip pin 10 is the 10th leg from the left on the bottom row.
Either crystal leg is fine — it has no + or −.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 10 to the crystal.

steps.clip: Push a 22 pF capacitor (marked “22”) in: one leg in the same column as the crystal's left leg, the other leg two columns to the left.
hints: It helps the crystal start and keep a steady beat.
It works either way round.
steps.goal: Put a 22 pF capacitor on the crystal's left leg.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the capacitor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Each crystal leg gets its own 22 pF capacitor to GND.
steps.goal: Connect the capacitor's other leg to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 22 pF capacitor (marked “22”) in: one leg in the same column as the crystal's right leg, the other leg two columns to the right.
hints: It helps the crystal start and keep a steady beat.
It works either way round.
steps.goal: Put a 22 pF capacitor on the crystal's right leg.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the capacitor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Each crystal leg gets its own 22 pF capacitor to GND.
steps.goal: Connect the capacitor's other leg to GND.

steps.clip: Run a wire from pin 13 on the Arduino to chip pin 19 (SCK).
hints: SCK is the clock: the Arduino ticks it for every bit it sends. Use exactly this pin.
Chip pin 19 is on the top row.
steps.goal: Connect pin 13 to chip pin 19.

steps.clip: Run a wire from pin 12 on the Arduino to chip pin 18 (MISO).
hints: MISO carries bits from the chip back to the Arduino. Use exactly this pin.
Chip pin 18 is on the top row.
steps.goal: Connect pin 12 to chip pin 18.

steps.clip: Run a wire from pin 11 on the Arduino to chip pin 17 (MOSI).
hints: MOSI carries bits from the Arduino to the chip. Use exactly this pin.
Chip pin 17 is on the top row.
steps.goal: Connect pin 11 to chip pin 17.

steps.clip: Run a wire from pin 10 on the Arduino to chip pin 1 (RESET).
hints: Pin 10 holds the chip in reset while it is being programmed. Use exactly this pin.
Chip pin 1 is on the bottom row.
steps.goal: Connect pin 10 to chip pin 1.

steps.clip: Push the 10 µF capacitor (the small can) in, its legs in two columns next to each other — the short leg, by the pale stripe, on the right.
hints: It only works one way round: the stripe marks the − leg.
steps.goal: Put the 10 µF capacitor on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the capacitor's long leg to RESET on the Arduino.
hints: RESET is on the Arduino's power header, next to 3.3V.
It stops the Arduino restarting itself when the computer starts talking to it.
steps.goal: Connect the long leg to RESET.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the capacitor's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: The short leg is −.
steps.goal: Connect the short leg to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the green LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the resistor you just placed to pin 9 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg. Use exactly this pin — the code counts through the pins in order.
Pin 9 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect the resistor to pin 9.

steps.clip: Put the green LED in: the long leg in the same column as that resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the green LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the green LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: The short leg is − (the cathode).
GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the green LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the red LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the resistor you just placed to pin 8 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg. Use exactly this pin — the code counts through the pins in order.
Pin 8 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect the resistor to pin 8.

steps.clip: Put the red LED in: the long leg in the same column as that resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the red LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the red LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: The short leg is − (the cathode).
GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the red LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the yellow LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the resistor you just placed to pin 7 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg. Use exactly this pin — the code counts through the pins in order.
Pin 7 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect the resistor to pin 7.

steps.clip: Put the yellow LED in: the long leg in the same column as that resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the yellow LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the yellow LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: The short leg is − (the cathode).
GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the yellow LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip:
Program the chip in four steps:
1. Pull the 10 µF capacitor out for a moment. Open File › Examples › 11.ArduinoISP › ArduinoISP (the same code as here) and click Upload. Put the capacitor back.
2. Tools › Board: Arduino Uno. Tools › Programmer: Arduino as ISP.
3. Tools › Burn Bootloader. The green LED breathes slowly while the programmer runs, the yellow one flickers while it writes, and the red one lights if something goes wrong.
4. Open File › Examples › 01.Basics › Blink and choose Sketch › Upload Using Programmer: the chip now has Blink. Keep it for the next level.
